title: Cast-Iron Architecture in New York: A Photographic Survey

description.main: Text by the preservationist Margot Gayle and photographs by Edmund V. Gillon Jr. survey New York's nineteenth-century cast-iron building fronts.
description.extended:
A photographic survey of New York's cast-iron building fronts, with text by the preservationist Margot Gayle and photographs by Edmund V. Gillon Jr.

Dover issued it in 1974 as a 190-page illustrated paperback with indexes, and the cover counts 217 illustrations. The photographs record the nineteenth-century iron façades of the city's commercial buildings.

Gayle (1908–2008) founded the Friends of Cast Iron Architecture in 1970 during the fight against Robert Moses's proposed expressway through TriBeCa and SoHo. The expressway was abandoned in 1971, and the 26-block SoHo Cast Iron Historic District was established in 1973, a year before this book appeared. She later wrote Cast Iron Architecture in America (1998) with Carol Gayle.
